votes.reason: At 38.3x trailing it is not cheap on its face, but 83.1% EPS growth more than covers that multiple for a sound, cash-generating business, and a flat 12-week return (-0.49%) means the book is not paying up after a run.

At 35.4x trailing against only 23.5% EPS growth, CAT has the highest multiple for its growth of any name on the sheet, and paying that much for a heavy-machinery cyclical on what the draft calls a record quarter leaves no margin of safety for a 25% position in a week when a hot CPI would hit high multiples first.

My own pick and the cheapest sound business in the book: 17.8x trailing on EPS up 112% after a 10.65% fall over 12 weeks, backed by a cash-rich balance sheet, even allowing that some of that EPS jump may be investment gains rather than operating profit.
My own pick: at 11.4x trailing with EPS up 10.1% it is the cheapest name on the sheet, a disciplined, sound underwriter that steadies the book if CPI runs hot.

30.5x trailing is a full price for a copper miner after a 10.76% rise over 12 weeks, but 55.1% EPS growth covers the multiple and the 10% weight limits the damage if copper turns, so I have no concrete value reason to block it.
